summary:
Set 127 Session 3 is the set-terminal session, and it closes the third surface answering the question the set exists for -- where is this session right now. Sessions 1 and 2 put the derived active step and its start time on the CLI checklist and in the Work Explorer. This session removes the failure mode on the step checklist's post at a verification-round boundary.

(1) THE PROBLEM WAS STRUCTURAL, NOT DISCIPLINARY. `check_checklist_posted` enforces the cadence positionally: for transitions t1 < t2 < ... < tk, each ti needs a post in [ti, ti+1). One transition type could not realistically be met. A blocking discovery round forces discovery -> supplementary -> remediate -> remediation-review in immediate succession -- minutes apart, machine-driven, orchestrator mid-remediation, nobody at the terminal. Set 126 S2 missed rounds 2 and 3 exactly that way and it was not the first; a miss cannot be repaired (you cannot post into the past), so the only exit is an operator-attested waiver. A recurring, structurally predictable omission was landing on the operator's desk as paperwork.

(2) THE FIX IS REMOVAL, NOT MORE DISCIPLINE (project-guidance: prefer removal over addition when fixing). `verify_session.post_round_checklist()` renders the checklist at the end of every round that COMPLETED and records it through the existing `record_post` path, so the record still means 'a render happened' -- no synthetic post records, which the spec forbids -- and the round's output becomes more informative rather than less. It is called from exactly one place: the line immediately after `record_round_completed()` in `run()`. That adjacency is the mechanism: every path that does not complete a round has already returned above it (refused past its bound -> EXIT_USAGE pre-call; --dry-run -> EXIT_OK before routing; first-call route failure -> EXIT_ROUTE_FAILED; verification_unavailable; a drifted-template stamp refusal), and a CLOSE-BACKSTOP round never enters `run()` at all because `close_backstop.py` calls the ledger writer directly -- consistent with `_checklist_transitions` already skipping backstop rounds, whose post window opens after the last moment anyone could post into it. Both failure modes (an unimportable/unrenderable checklist; a refused ledger append) fail OPEN and are NAMED on stderr (L-079-1): bookkeeping appended after a metered call must never turn a round the operator has already paid for into a failure, and a silent skip would be the invisible omission the whole mechanism exists to end.

(3) THE GATE LOSES A FAILURE MODE, NOT A CHECK. `check_checklist_posted` is unchanged in behaviour -- same positional windows, same one-post-per-window rule, same waiver path, still advisory per the Set 116 S3 operator ruling. It still derives round transitions from `sN-rounds.jsonl` and still applies the windows to them; the change could have been implemented inside the gate by excusing the round transition, and deliberately was not, because excusing it would also excuse a round the tool FAILED to post for. Every other transition type -- session start, test-run recorded, operator stop, last logged step -- binds exactly as it did, and those are the ones a human can actually hit.

(4) THIS WAS NOT SELF-AUTHORIZED. Reducing what a close-time gate can catch is the decision-rights hard carve-out that `decision_journal` refuses to let the orchestrator take. The spec required the mechanism ratified BEFORE the session started, and it was: journalled at registration, before any implementation, with authority=human, rubric_line=escalate-to-human, verification_effect=reduces, and both rejected options recorded with their consequences (orchestrator discipline only -- the evidence says it decays; re-arm the gate as blocking -- would have refused Set 126 S2's close over paperwork the orchestrator could not have filed). The cost is stated plainly in the authoring guide, the gate docstring and the changelog: that transition can no longer be missed, so it can no longer report a missing post.

(5) FALSIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND PROVEN TO BITE. `TestRoundBoundaryPostsItsOwnChecklist` is 9 functions (spec irony budget: 8). FIRES: the Set 126 S2 sequence -- discovery -> supplementary -> remediation-review back to back, all three blocking -- leaves exactly one post inside each round's own positional window and `check_checklist_posted` returns ok; and the post is a real render through the existing writer (the rendered block appears on stdout, the record carries surface and stepCount). DOES NOT FIRE: --dry-run, a refused past-the-bound round, a failed routed call, and a close-backstop round each record nothing; and the other transition types still bind (an unposted test-run transition is still reported, with no round transition named). STRUCTURAL: the one-post-per-window rule asserted against a HAND-BUILT ledger rather than by reading the new call site -- the test that would go green for the wrong reason if auto-posting had been implemented by widening the window. Plus the named fail-open. Seven defects were then planted against the finished suite and EVERY ONE was caught (L-112-1): the call deleted (4 failures), posting before the round exists so --dry-run and a failed route post too (4), the LEDGER WRITER posting so a backstop round posts too (3), the gate excusing round transitions (1), the window widened to 'any later post covers it' (1), the render happening but never recorded (3), and the fail-open skip made silent (1). The harness lived outside the repo, patched one file at a time and reverted; `git status` is clean of it.

(6) THE CADENCE DOCUMENTATION WAS CORRECTED TO MATCH THE MECHANISM. An instruction that survives the change it describes is the defect family Set 126 spent a session on. Three surfaces: the constitution's Step 4 transition list, the authoring guide's step-checklist cadence table (plus a block stating the automation, its bounds and the ratified cost), and `check_checklist_posted`'s own docstring. The constitution's edit made Step 4 SHORTER, not longer -- the file sits at its 4,000-token preload ceiling and ceilings ratchet down only, so the removed obligation paid for the sentence that replaced it (verified with `guidance_report --check`, which refused a first draft at +18 tokens). Two stale `<- here` claims in the guide, left behind by the Set 120 S3 operator ruling, went in the same pass (L-069-1: a consistency fix is global, not point-local).

(7) SET-TERMINAL DELIVERABLES. `docs/planning/work-explorer-in-progress-step-icon.md` moves from 'diagnosed, not fixed' to FIXED, citing the three sessions that closed it, stating that no writer was added so every historical set is fixed retroactively, and recording the deliberate NON-backfill of the five prose-in-`status` rows together with the obligation they actually create (the derivation must not trust the status field blindly -- and does not: it reads whether an entry EXISTS, pinned by Set 127 S2's corpus case). `change-log.md` covers all three sessions. `ai_router/CHANGELOG.md` gains a Set 127 [Unreleased] entry for the S1 and S3 router work (S2's extension work is in the extension changelog, which S2 wrote). Step 9 guidance review: NO CHANGES RECOMMENDED -- all four preload files are at 99-100% of their ceilings, and the candidate lesson from this session ('when an obligation depends on a human being present during a machine-driven sequence, remove the obligation rather than re-teach it') is already the project-guidance principle 'prefer removal over addition when fixing', which this session cited and applied rather than restated.

VERIFICATION: round 1 discovery, fan-out 2 (spec-conformance + failure-scenario lenses, both gpt-5.5, anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's effective provider): VERIFIED, 0 blocking, 0 minor. The round's own output shows the new mechanism working in production -- the checklist rendered and recorded at the round boundary, which is the post that covers `verification-round 1`.

TWO SELF-CAUGHT RESIDUALS, RECORDED NOT BURIED. (a) `s3-conventions.md` describes the operator's reading order as 'what happened -> where the session is -> what to do next'; the actual print order is checklist -> round summary -> next action, i.e. the first two are inverted. The substantive claim in that bullet (the adjacency, and that the summary and Next action print after the checklist) is correct. It was found after the round returned, and `s3-conventions.md` is NOT in WORK_DIFF_SET_BOOKKEEPING, so editing it would have staled a passing stamp and sent the close backstop into a fresh metered round to fix a reading-order arrow -- left as written, which is also the honest record of what the verifier was shown. (b) The pytest run of record was recorded without `--session-number`, so it carries no session attribution and derives no test-run checklist transition for session 3. `test_run_fresh` passes regardless and the window it would have opened was covered anyway (a post landed 7 seconds after the record), but it is worth noting that `run_of_record record` accepts an unattributed run silently, and an unattributed record removes an obligation rather than adding one -- a small sharp edge for whoever next touches that CLI. STEP 9 ADDENDUM -- cite_lessons flagged L-069-1, L-064-10 and L-095-1 as ARCHIVED with a reconsider-reactivating prompt. Answer: NO, and it is the same answer for all three. Each is archived precisely because it was PROMOTED -- its canonical rule now lives in project-guidance.md, which is itself preload -- so reactivating the active-tier copy would restore the redundancy Sets 073 and 110 removed, and would do it into a file already at 100%% of its ceiling. The citation still did its job: last-used-set is bumped, so the usage signal that drives future archival decisions is recorded without moving any text.

uat.attestation: Operator walked s2-uat-walk.md on 2026-08-12 -- the operator who reported the defect, on the surface they reported it against -- and answered all three items. LOOK 1 (can you tell where the session is, and how long it has been there, from two feet away, without reading a row?): "Yes." PASS. DECIDE A (start time only, no end time, no date handling): "Keep as is -- start time with the dash after it is great." The trailing dash reads as a start rather than a completion, which was the whole reason for it. DECIDE B (a step that has not started shows no time): "Keep it blank." Both Decide answers ratify the rulings taken at spec authoring and journalled at Session 1 registration with uat_decide: true, now confirmed against the rendered result rather than in the abstract. No defects found and no changes requested. uatScope is per-set, so this one walk discharges the whole set; the walk was authored in Session 2 against a fixture that was first given a seeded plan so it could actually show the feature, with its rendered rows pinned by a Layer 2 test through the real scan (project-guidance: UAT is pre-verified by automation). The answers are recorded HERE rather than filled into s2-uat-walk.md in place: that file is not in WORK_DIFF_SET_BOOKKEEPING, so editing it after a passing round would have staled the stamp and sent the close backstop into a fresh metered round to record three answers.
